albums.blurb: e.s.t. — the Swedish trio of pianist Esbjörn Svensson, bassist Dan Berglund and drummer Magnus Öström — spent the 1990s building a following at home before this, their first album released internationally on Munich's ACT label. It set the template the group refined until Svensson's death in 2008: acoustic piano-trio jazz shaped by pop structures, rock dynamics and discreet electronics, all of it instrumental, with the closer "Dodge the Dodo" becoming the band's signature piece.
albums.reception: The album was e.s.t.'s international breakthrough: Süddeutsche Zeitung called it "a little miracle", and ACT credits its sessions with producing the first Swedish jazz video shown on MTV.

albums.blurb: Kendrick Lamar's second studio album and his major-label debut on Top Dawg/Aftermath/Interscope, subtitled "a short film by Kendrick Lamar". It is a concept record following one day in his teenage life in Compton — cruising in his mother's van, peer pressure, a robbery gone wrong — told out of sequence and stitched together with voicemail skits, and it sits between the independent Section.80 and the jazz-saturated To Pimp a Butterfly in his discography.
albums.reception: It debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 with about 242,000 first-week sales, the biggest debut for a new artist in 2012 at the time, and later became the first hip-hop studio album to spend ten years on that chart.

albums.blurb: Phoenix formed in Versailles in the 1990s, part of the same suburban scene that produced Air and Daft Punk — guitarist Laurent Brancowitz played alongside the future Daft Punk duo in the band Darlin' before joining. Wolfgang Amadeus Phoenix is their fourth album, the record that turned a decade-old cult band into an arena act on the back of the singles "1901" and "Lisztomania" and Thomas Mars's clipped, bright vocal delivery.
albums.reception: The album won the 2010 Grammy Award for Best Alternative Music Album, and "1901" reached No. 1 on Billboard's Alternative Songs chart.
